Dhaka, 20 August 2026: The Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) participated in the Fifth Bangladesh-China Renewable Energy Forum, titled “Industrial Rooftop Solar in RMG Sector: Investment Potential for Chinese FDI,” organized by the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD).

The forum focused on the significant potential of industrial rooftop solar in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector and explored opportunities for attracting Chinese foreign direct investment (FDI), financing, technology, and expertise to accelerate the adoption of rooftop solar.

The discussion brought together policymakers, industry representatives, investors, financiers, technology providers, EPC companies, researchers, and other relevant stakeholders to exchange perspectives on the opportunities and challenges associated with scaling up industrial rooftop solar in Bangladesh.

Engr. Zahidul Alam, Senior Vice President of BSREA, participated in the forum as a Distinguished Discussant. He shared valuable insights from the perspective of the renewable energy industry and contributed to discussions on the practical challenges, investment environment, and policy measures required to unlock the full potential of rooftop solar in the RMG sector.

The forum also highlighted the importance of reliable data, appropriate financing mechanisms, supportive policies, and stronger institutional coordination in attracting domestic and foreign investment into Bangladesh’s industrial rooftop solar market.

BSREA believes that industrial rooftop solar can play an important role in supporting the country’s clean energy transition while helping industries improve energy security, reduce their environmental footprint, and remain competitive in the global market.

title: BSREA President Highlights Solar Energy Potential and Policy Challenges at FERB Seminar
excerpt: The Forum for Energy Reporters Bangladesh (FERB) organized a seminar titled “Energy Sector Crisis: Prospects and Ways Forward”, bringing together policymakers, energy experts, academics, and industry representatives to discuss the challenges and future direction of Bangladesh’s energy sector. content:
The Forum for Energy Reporters Bangladesh (FERB) organized a seminar titled “Energy Sector Crisis: Prospects and Ways Forward”, bringing together policymakers, energy experts, academics, and industry representatives to discuss the challenges and future direction of Bangladesh’s energy sector.

The seminar was attended by the Honourable Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, Mr. Iqbal Hasan Mahmud Tuku, MP, as the Chief Guest, while the Honourable State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources, Mr. Anindya Islam Amit, MP, attended as the Special Guest.

Mostafa Al Mahmud, President of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA), participated in the seminar as a representative of the renewable energy sector. In his remarks, he highlighted the significant potential of solar energy in addressing the country’s energy challenges, while also drawing attention to several policy and implementation barriers currently affecting the renewable energy industry.

He emphasized that if Bangladesh can provide affordable solar electricity to two crore households, the country could significantly reduce the burden of the current load-shedding situation.

The BSREA President also raised concerns regarding the challenges faced by businesses following the announcement of the national budget. He noted that a number of renewable energy-related shipments remain stuck at ports due to customs-related complications, preventing businesses from receiving the duty benefits announced by the government. As a result, many businesses are facing significant difficulties and uncertainty.

While appreciating the government’s commitment to renewable energy and the incentives and facilities announced in the national budget, Mr. Al Mahmud pointed out that bureaucratic and procedural complexities are preventing the effective implementation of these initiatives. Despite reductions in customs duties announced for various renewable energy products and components, businesses are reportedly still required to pay duties of up to 17% in some cases to release their products.

In response to the concerns raised by the BSREA President, the Honourable Minister and State Minister assured participants that stakeholders facing such challenges could submit the relevant documents to the Ministry. They stated that the issues would be reviewed and that necessary steps would be taken to resolve them.

Earlier in his remarks, the Honourable Minister reiterated the government’s commitment to implementing the duty exemptions and other facilities announced in the national budget for solar energy and the wider renewable energy sector. He further assured that if any procedural complications were hindering implementation, the government would take prompt measures to address them.

The discussion highlighted the importance of ensuring the effective implementation of policy incentives and regulatory support to accelerate the growth of renewable energy in Bangladesh. Expanding access to affordable solar power, reducing administrative barriers, and creating a more supportive business environment will be essential for strengthening the country’s energy security and building a sustainable energy future.

Munir, Company Secretary, delivered a presentation titled “Challenges Faced by EPCs and Industry Actors.” During his presentation, he outlined the key barriers affecting Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) companies and other industry stakeholders, including policy inconsistencies, implementation challenges, financing constraints, and the need for a more supportive business environment to accelerate distributed renewable energy deployment in Bangladesh.

Through its participation, BSREA reiterated the importance of coordinated policy reforms, effective implementation mechanisms, and stronger public-private collaboration to unlock the full potential of distributed renewable energy and support Bangladesh’s clean energy transition.

title: BSREA and DCCI Sign MoU to Accelerate Sustainable Energy and Green Industrialization in Bangladesh
excerpt: The Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) and the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce & Industry (DCCI) have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in promoting sustainable energy, green industrialization, and increased private sector engagement in Bangladesh. The MoU signing ceremony was held in Dhaka on 27 June 2026. On behalf…
content:
The Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) and the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce & Industry (DCCI) have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to strengthen collaboration in promoting sustainable energy, green industrialization, and increased private sector engagement in Bangladesh.

The MoU signing ceremony was held in Dhaka on 27 June 2026. On behalf of BSREA, the agreement was signed by Engr. Md. Ataur Rahman Sarker (Rojel), General Secretary, while Dr. A.K.M. Asaduzzaman Pathowary, Acting Secretary General signed on behalf of DCCI.

This strategic partnership aims to foster cooperation in advancing renewable energy adoption through research, policy dialogue, knowledge exchange, capacity building, and advocacy initiatives. Special emphasis will be placed on facilitating access to green energy solutions for Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) and encouraging private sector participation.

Under the agreement, BSREA and DCCI will jointly work on:

  • Research, market analysis, and knowledge initiatives on renewable energy and the green economy
  • Organizing seminars, workshops, webinars, conferences, and roadshows
  • Policy recommendations and dialogues to support a business- and investment-friendly environment
  • Capacity-building initiatives for professionals, entrepreneurs, researchers, and policymakers
  • Expanding green energy adoption across SMEs
  • Promoting renewable energy, energy efficiency, and innovative technologies
  • Conducting joint research, pilot projects, and advocacy initiatives to address sector challenges

Both organizations believe that expanding renewable energy adoption is essential for Bangladesh’s sustainable economic development, energy security, industrial competitiveness, and climate resilience.

To support implementation, a Joint Working Group will be formed to develop action plans, oversee activities, and monitor progress under the partnership.

Through this collaboration, BSREA and DCCI aim to unlock new opportunities for green investment, innovation, and sustainable private sector growth while contributing to Bangladesh’s broader green transition journey.

title: BSREA Reviews National Budget 2026–27, Calls for Inclusive Renewable Energy Policies
excerpt: Today, the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) organized a press conference to present its observations and assessment on the National Budget 2026–27 and the recent SROs related to the renewable energy sector. While the national budget and subsequent announcements created optimism around the expansion of renewable energy in Bangladesh, BSREA’s review indicates that…
content:
Today, the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) organized a press conference to present its observations and assessment on the National Budget 2026–27 and the recent SROs related to the renewable energy sector.

While the national budget and subsequent announcements created optimism around the expansion of renewable energy in Bangladesh, BSREA’s review indicates that the announced tax and duty incentives are currently being implemented within a limited framework and are not yet equally accessible across the broader renewable energy value chain.

During the press conference, BSREA highlighted that Bangladesh’s renewable energy market has been built through the collective contribution of importers, EPC companies, distributors, technology providers, investors, businesses, and millions of residential, commercial, agricultural, and industrial consumers. A policy environment that benefits only selected business models may limit wider market participation and slow the country’s renewable energy transition.

BSREA emphasized the importance of creating a level playing field by ensuring equal policy support, encouraging both CAPEX and OPEX business models, promoting rooftop and distributed renewable energy solutions, and enabling broader access to clean energy technologies across all user groups.

The Association also stressed that accelerating renewable energy adoption is directly linked to strengthening national energy security, reducing dependence on imported fuels, supporting private sector investment, generating employment, improving industrial competitiveness, and advancing Bangladesh’s climate commitments.

BSREA remains committed to working collaboratively with government authorities, industry stakeholders, and development partners to ensure that renewable energy policies create opportunities for all.

Renewable Energy for All, Not for a Few.

BSREA remains committed to advocating for practical policies and collaborative actions that will help accelerate Bangladesh’s clean energy transition.

Participants discussed the importance of ensuring a competitive fiscal framework, attracting both local and foreign investment, and addressing regulatory challenges that may hinder the expansion of clean energy technologies.

BSREA emphasized that a supportive customs and tax regime is essential for promoting renewable energy adoption, encouraging private sector participation, and achieving the country’s long-term energy transition goals. The Association also highlighted the role of renewable energy in strengthening energy security, generating employment opportunities, and supporting sustainable economic development.

The Canadian delegation was represented by Debra Boyce, Counsellor and Senior Trade Commissioner, and Quazi Gulam Farhad, Trade Commissioner. Key Areas of Discussion

  • Clean and Renewable Energy Collaboration: Exploring joint initiatives in solar, wind, and other sustainable energy solutions.
  • Technology Transfer and Innovation: Facilitating access to advanced Canadian technologies and expertise to support Bangladesh’s energy goals.
  • Investment Opportunities: Highlighting Bangladesh as a growing market for renewable energy investments and partnerships.
  • Capacity Building and Workforce Development: Strengthening technical skills and knowledge exchange to support long-term sector growth.
Future Partnerships and MoU Prospects

BSREA expressed strong interest in establishing formal institutional partnerships with Canadian renewable energy stakeholders. A potential Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was discussed as a pathway to enhance:

  • Business networking opportunities
  • Knowledge sharing platforms
  • Industry collaboration and engagement

Such partnerships are expected to create tangible benefits for BSREA members while fostering deeper international cooperation.

Driving a Sustainable Energy Future

This engagement reflects BSREA’s ongoing commitment to building global partnerships that support Bangladesh’s transition to a sustainable, low-carbon energy system. Strengthening ties with Canada opens new avenues for innovation, investment, and capacity development—key pillars for achieving long-term energy security and climate goals.

As Bangladesh continues to expand its renewable energy landscape, collaborations like this play a vital role in accelerating progress and creating impactful opportunities across the sector.

title: Domestic Solar Power Key to Solving Bangladesh’s Energy Crisis: Insights from Press Briefing
excerpt: A sustainable and long-term solution to Bangladesh’s ongoing energy challenges lies in scaling up domestic solar power, according to experts at a recent press briefing held on 4 May at the National Press Club. The briefing was jointly organized by the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA), ActionAid Bangladesh, and JETnet-BD, bringing together civil…
content:
A sustainable and long-term solution to Bangladesh’s ongoing energy challenges lies in scaling up domestic solar power, according to experts at a recent press briefing held on 4 May at the National Press Club.

The briefing was jointly organized by the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA), ActionAid Bangladesh, and JETnet-BD, bringing together civil society representatives, energy experts, and stakeholders to discuss Bangladesh’s renewable energy future.

10,000 MW Solar Target: A Realistic Path Forward

Speakers welcomed the government’s target of generating 10,000 MW of solar power by 2030, describing it as both timely and achievable. However, they emphasized that meeting this target will require a transparent, inclusive, and sustainable implementation roadmap supported by strong policy alignment and financial commitment.

Key Recommendations for Advancing Energy Sovereignty

During the discussion, experts outlined several strategic recommendations to accelerate Bangladesh’s transition toward renewable energy:

Integrated Solar Expansion
A comprehensive approach is needed to rapidly scale up solar deployment across multiple segments, including off-grid and community-based systems, rooftop solar, solar irrigation, as well as innovative solutions such as agro-voltaics and floating solar projects.

Reducing Dependence on Imported Fuels
Bangladesh currently spends significant foreign exchange on LNG and coal imports. Expanding domestic renewable energy has the potential to save billions of dollars while enhancing energy security and resilience.

Ensuring a Just Energy Transition
A people-centered approach is critical. Experts stressed the importance of including marginalized communities and women in the energy transition process to ensure equity and shared benefits.

Policy Reform and Investment Support
To unlock the full potential of renewable energy, it is essential to address existing barriers such as high import duties, policy constraints, and financing gaps. Creating an enabling environment will attract investment and accelerate clean energy adoption.

Strengthening Bangladesh’s Energy Future

The discussions highlighted that reducing reliance on imported fuels and prioritizing domestic renewable resources—particularly solar energy—can play a transformative role in strengthening Bangladesh’s economic stability and energy independence.

As BSREA, we remain committed to advancing sustainable energy solutions, policy advocacy, and stakeholder collaboration to support Bangladesh’s journey toward a cleaner, more resilient, and inclusive energy future.

The association stressed that the current crisis presents a critical opportunity for Bangladesh to shift towards a more sustainable, resilient, and self-reliant energy future.

The Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) in collaboration with the Dhaka Chamber of Commerce & Industry (DCCI) and Infrastructure Development Company Limited (IDCOL), successfully organized a roundtable discussion titled “Navigating the Global Energy Shock: Impact on Bangladesh and Way Forward” on Thursday, 09 April 2026, at the DCCI Auditorium, Motijheel, Dhaka.

The roundtable was convened at a critical time when Bangladesh is grappling with a fragile macroeconomic environment, compounded by global energy market volatility and supply chain disruptions, particularly in key transit routes such as the Strait of Hormuz. These external shocks have significantly increased fuel import costs, intensified energy shortages, and placed considerable strain on industrial productivity, foreign exchange reserves, and overall economic stability.

Bringing together policymakers, industry leaders, energy experts, and private sector representatives, the discussion provided a platform to critically assess the multidimensional impacts of the ongoing global energy crisis on Bangladesh. Participants highlighted the “double squeeze” of rising energy prices and constrained supply, which is forcing difficult policy choices between increased subsidies and inflationary pressures.

The session focused on identifying immediate response strategies to mitigate the current crisis, while also exploring long-term solutions for strengthening energy security. Key recommendations included reducing dependency on imported fossil fuels, accelerating renewable energy adoption, enhancing energy efficiency, and fostering greater public-private collaboration in the energy sector.

Distinguished discussants shared valuable insights and practical perspectives on navigating the evolving global energy landscape. The dialogue emphasized the urgent need for strategic policy interventions and investment in sustainable energy solutions to ensure resilience and long-term economic stability.

The roundtable concluded with a strong call for coordinated action among stakeholders to transform current challenges into opportunities, paving the way for a more secure, diversified, and sustainable energy future for Bangladesh.

title: Courtesy Meeting with State Minister Anindya Islam Amit
excerpt: A delegation from the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) paid a courtesy visit to Anindya Islam Amit, Honorable State Minister of the Ministry of Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources. content:
A delegation from the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) paid a courtesy visit to Anindya Islam Amit, Honorable State Minister of the Ministry of Power, Energy, and Mineral Resources.

During the meeting, BSREA representatives exchanged views on the expansion of renewable energy, sustainable power development, and the future potential of Bangladesh’s clean energy sector. The delegation also presented several key issues and recommendations aimed at accelerating the country’s renewable energy transition.

Key issues and recommendations included:

Rooftop Solar Expansion: Unlocking 3,000–4,000 MW potential from industrial, commercial, and residential rooftops through supportive policies and financing.

Utility-Scale Solar and Wind Projects: Identifying non-agricultural government land and allocating projects through transparent competitive bidding to reduce electricity generation costs.

Review of Pending Renewable Projects: Conducting transparent reviews of previously approved LOIs and fast-tracking projects without irregularities to quickly add clean electricity to the national grid.

Solar Irrigation Expansion: Gradually replacing diesel-powered irrigation pumps with solar systems to reduce diesel imports and save foreign exchange.

River-Based Solar Development: Exploring solar installations on major rivers such as the Jamuna, integrating renewable energy development with river management, fisheries, and navigation.

Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS): Encouraging deployment of energy storage to support grid stability and renewable energy integration.

Investment-Friendly Policy Environment: Ensuring bankable Power Purchase Agreements (PPA) and Implementation Agreements (IA) to attract international investors.

Strengthening Institutional Capacity: Enhancing the role of Sustainable and Renewable Energy Development Authority (SREDA) to accelerate renewable energy policy implementation and market development.

Electric Vehicle (EV) Integration: Promoting EV adoption and solar-powered charging infrastructure to reduce fossil fuel dependence.

Supportive Fiscal Measures: Recommending tax and duty reductions, concessional financing, and expansion of net metering to encourage renewable energy investment.

BSREA reaffirmed its commitment to working closely with the government and stakeholders to advance a clean, secure, and sustainable energy future for Bangladesh.

-Joint research and knowledge exchange
-Climate and energy finance innovation
-Gender-responsive and community-centered energy planning
-Promotion of distributed and decentralized solar models

The partnership is non-financial and non-exclusive in nature, focusing on advisory, facilitative, and advocacy-oriented collaboration. It reflects a shared vision of accelerating Bangladesh’s clean energy transition while ensuring energy access, affordability, community resilience, and decent livelihoods.

Through this collaboration, BSREA and ActionAid Bangladesh reaffirm their commitment to fostering sustainable development and building a greener, fairer, and more resilient Bangladesh.

content: On 3 February 2026, the Virtual Kick-off Workshop on the Development of Operation & Maintenance (O&M) Guidelines for Solar Projects in Bangladesh took place, jointly organized by GIZ Bangladesh Energy Cluster, SREDA, and the Power Division, MPEMR, under the Green Energy Transition – Policy Advisory Partnership (GET-PAP) project.With over 80 participants from government institutions, the private sector, utilities, development partners, financial institutions, industry associations, and academia, the workshop marked a significant step toward strengthening the long-term performance and reliability of Bangladesh’s rapidly expanding solar sector. Mr Muhammad Khalequzzaman, Joint Secretary, Energy Efficiency & Conservation Branch, Power Division, MPEMR, chaired the event. Mr Mostafa Al Mahmud, President, BSREA, was present as a project partner. The Chief Guest Mr Muzaffar Ahmed, stated, “As Bangladesh rapidly scales up grid-connected rooftop, hybrid, and utility-scale solar projects, the focus is shifting from installation to long-term sustainability through energy efficiency and renewable energy development.”Mr Muhammad Khalequzzaman, emphasized, “The development of national O&M guidelines is timely and essential to standardize best practices and protect long-term investments in the solar sector.”Mr Edwin Koekkoek, said, “These workshops are not only about producing guidelines, but also about knowledge exchange and strengthening connections between European and Bangladeshi companies.”Mr Mostafa Al Mahmud, President, BSREA, highlighted Bangladesh’s remarkable solar journey — “Bangladesh has emerged as a global leader in solar energy, with over six million solar home systems installed and ambitious renewable energy targets for 2030 and 2040.”The workshop provided a clear overview of the guideline development framework, stakeholder roles, and the collaborative approach required to ensure that solar projects across Bangladesh deliver safe, efficient, and reliable performance throughout their lifecycle.

title: Expanding Renewable Energy Is Now a National Necessity to Ensure Energy Security and Sustainability – BSREA
excerpt: To ensure energy security and long-term sustainability in the power sector, the expansion of renewable energy has become a necessity, according to the Bangladesh Solar and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA). The organization has presented several recommendations and proposals to the government in this regard. These suggestions were shared during a press conference held on Saturday…
content:
To ensure energy security and long-term sustainability in the power sector, the expansion of renewable energy has become a necessity, according to the Bangladesh Solar and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA). The organization has presented several recommendations and proposals to the government in this regard.

These suggestions were shared during a press conference held on Saturday (July 5) at the Dhaka Reporters Unity.

Speakers at the event said that as the country’s natural gas reserves are gradually depleting, the energy sector is becoming increasingly import-dependent, putting pressure on foreign exchange reserves. Therefore, expanding renewable energy is now a timely and essential step.

They stated, “We want a stable, investment-friendly environment where both international and local investors feel confident, and where the country’s renewable energy sector can develop into a reliable destination for future investments.”

BSREA’s Key Recommendations:

  1. The government has already invited tenders for 55 new solar power projects, which is a positive move. However, the participation of foreign investors in these projects is still below expectations. Some projects have received only a single bidder, while others have received none. The earlier cancellation of 37 solar power projects has created a sense of distrust among investors. Those cancelled projects had already seen investments of around USD 300 million. Therefore, BSREA urges the government to reconsider and review the cancelled projects.
  2. Ensure tax benefits for OPEX-based investments to enable power producers to expand renewable energy affordably and effectively over the long term.
  3. High tariffs on solar equipment must be reduced to form a unified and supportive duty structure.
  4. The net metering process must be made more transparent, simplified, and investor-friendly.
  5. Existing import duties on lithium-ion battery cells should be reduced.
  6. In line with the High Court’s directive, a dedicated cell under the Ministry of Power should be formed to ensure solar panels are installed on all rooftops across the country.

Attendees at the Press Conference:

Among others, the event was attended by BSREA General Secretary Engr. Ataur Rahman Sarkar Rozel, Senior Vice President Zahidul Alam, Abu Taher, Sheikh Mohammad Ruhul Amin, and Finance Director Nitai Pada Saha.

Source: Bangla Tribune

content:
We are delighted to announce that the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association (BSREA) and the NSEFI – National Solar Energy Federation of India (NSEFI) have officially signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to advance regional collaboration in the field of sustainable and renewable energy.

The MoU was signed by Mr. Mostafa Al Mahmud, President of BSREA, and Mr. Subrahmanyam Pulipaka, CEO of NSEFI, marking a significant milestone in cross-border cooperation on clean energy.

This partnership is the result of a series of positive discussions that began with a virtual meeting on May 30, 2025, facilitated by Ms. Muskaan Sethi, Manager – International Relations & Cooperation at NSEFI, and Advocate A.S.M Munir, Secretary of BSREA.

The primary objective of this partnership is to strengthen regional cooperation in the field of renewable energy by fostering institutional collaboration, knowledge exchange, and joint initiatives. The MoU emphasizes the following areas:

Exchange of knowledge, policy experiences, and regulatory frameworks;
Joint research, publications, and advocacy initiatives;
Capacity building, skill development, and technical cooperation;
Collaboration on regional projects, funding opportunities, and sectoral studies;
Joint organization and participation in workshops, trade fairs, conferences, and stakeholder forums;
Facilitating business linkages, industry matchmaking, and bilateral study tours.

Both sides are excited to now move forward with operationalizing the MoU through joint action planning, knowledge exchange, collaborative research, and capacity-building initiatives that will contribute to achieving regional renewable energy goals.

This partnership underscores a shared commitment to accelerating the clean energy transition across South Asia through cooperation, nnovation, and mutual support.

🤝 Together, BSREA and NSEFI stand united in shaping a sustainable energy future for the region.

Solar irrigation pumps are transforming the agricultural landscape in Bangladesh, offering a sustainable alternative to diesel-based systems and reducing dependency on grid electricity in remote areas. 🌾⚡

In a country where agriculture remains the backbone of rural livelihoods, solar pumps are enabling farmers to irrigate more efficiently, cut fuel costs, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions — all while increasing crop yields and incomes.

Thanks to strong support from development partners, government initiatives like IDCOL’s Solar Irrigation Program, and rising investor interest, solar-powered irrigation is rapidly expanding. This clean tech solution is proving vital for climate resilience, food security, and rural empowerment across Bangladesh.

As climate challenges intensify, expanding access to solar irrigation must be a priority — not just for economic development but for long-term sustainability.

The global momentum is clear: The solar pump market, valued at $1.2B in 2021, is set to reach $3.38B by 2031, growing at a CAGR of 11.1%. Bangladesh can—and must—lead from the front in this renewable revolution.

Let’s continue scaling clean, affordable, and farmer-friendly irrigation for a greener tomorrow.
